a.text: The main brownstone structure was completed.

b.text: The three-story brownstone for Hanover Bank was completed.

a.text: The brick structures at 60–64 Stone Street date to 1836.

b.text: The 60–66 Stone Street and 95–105 Pearl Street lots were redeveloped with four-story brick commercial structures.

a.text: The New York Cotton Exchange began occupying the building.

b.text: The Cotton Exchange quarters were officially opened.

a.text: The New York Cotton Exchange's occupancy of the building ended.

b.text: The Cotton Exchange officially moved to its new building.

a.text: The structures were purchased by the India House.

b.text: The India House was founded by James A. Farrell and Willard Straight.

a.text: The building was designated a city landmark by the LPC.

b.text: 1 Hanover Squares exterior was designated by the LPC as an official city landmark.

a.text: The building was added to the National Register of Historic Places.

b.text: Harry Poulakakos and his wife Adrienne opened Harry's Bar within the basement of 1 Hanover Square.

a.text: The India House club decided to renovate the exterior of 1 Hanover Square to plans by Nicholson & Galloway.

b.text: A maritime-themed park on Hanover Square was dedicated.
